text: The keystone arch is an ancient architectural feature. It is composed of congruent isosceles trapezoids fitted together along the non-parallel sides, as shown. The bottom sides of the two end trapezoids are horizontal. In an arch made with $9$ trapezoids, let $x$ be the angle measure in degrees of the larger interior angle of the trapezoid. What is $x$?
figure: A semicircular arch standing on a horizontal ground line, built from 9 congruent isosceles trapezoids placed side by side. Neighboring trapezoids share a leg (non-parallel side). The two end trapezoids stand on the ground line with their bottom sides lying along it; the middle (fifth) trapezoid sits at the top of the arch with its parallel sides horizontal. In each trapezoid the longer parallel side is on the outside of the arch and the shorter one on the inside. No angles or lengths are marked.
